newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura says regrets raid, to cooperate in probe.
newsitem.headline: Nomura says regrets raid, to cooperate in probe.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it regrets that its headquarters had been raided by prosecutors and officials from the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC).
Nomura also said in a statement that it would cooperate with the authorities in their investigation into suspected illegal transactions.
"We deeply regret that such a situation has come to pass," a Nomura spokesman said, reading from a company statement. "The company will continue to cooperate with relevant authorities."

Earlier on Tuesday, prosecutors and officials from the securities watchdog raided Nomura's main offices and a number of other locations as part of their investigations into suspect deals involving Nomura directors.

Nomura said earlier this month that two directors, who subsequently resigned, had made apparently illegal deals and funnelled funds to a corporate client linked by Japanese media to a former "sokaiya" racketeer.

Sokaiya, often linked to "yakuza" crime syndicates, typically try to extort money from firms by threatening to expose dubious business practices or to disturb shareholders' meetings -- called "sokai" in Japanese.
Prosecutors said on Tuesday that one of the directors had funnelled money to a company run by a relative of a sokaiya to ensure a Nomura shareholders' meeting went smoothly.
